lead: Protect your gains, mid-workout. 4 g of 2:1:1 BCAAs plus L-glutamine and B6 in a honeydew-watermelon scoop — to fuel your muscles, reduce breakdown during training and speed up recovery after. Sip it intra- or post-workout.
note: 45 servings · Honeydew Watermelon · 10.3 oz (292 g) · ships in 1–2 days

science.title: Why BCAAs during training
science.text: When you train hard — especially fasted or in a deficit — your body can start breaking down muscle for fuel. Branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) give your muscles the building blocks to keep going and rebuild instead. We use the research-backed 2:1:1 ratio, add L-glutamine for recovery and B6 to help amino-acid metabolism, so you train harder and bounce back faster.

format.title: Sip your recovery
format.text: A light, fruity honeydew-watermelon drink you sip during or after training — keeping aminos flowing when your muscles need them most. No sugar, no heaviness.
list: — 1/2 scoop (6.5 g) = 4 g BCAAs + 1 g glutamine

usage.title: Half a scoop, sip and train

steps.title: Half a scoop in water
steps.text: Mix 1/2 scoop (6.5 g) into 8–10 oz of cold water and shake — double it for a bigger 8 g BCAA dose.

steps.title: Sip during training
steps.text: Sip it through your workout to keep aminos topped up, or right after to kick-start recovery.

steps.title: Any training day
steps.text: Use it on any training day; it's stimulant-free, so the time of day doesn't matter.

items.a: The classic time is during ('intra') your workout to reduce muscle breakdown, or right after to support recovery. They're stimulant-free, so you can have them any time.
It's 2 parts leucine to 1 part each of isoleucine and valine — the ratio most studied for muscle protein synthesis, led by leucine, the key trigger amino acid.

items.q: Do I need this if I take protein?
items.a: If you eat plenty of protein you're getting BCAAs already. This is most useful for training fasted, in a calorie deficit, or for long sessions where you want aminos flowing without a full meal.

items.q: Why is there glutamine in it?
items.a: L-glutamine is the most abundant amino acid in muscle and supports recovery, the immune system and gut health — a useful addition after hard training.
Yes — the aminos are fermented (plant-based), it's coloured with beet and grape skin, and it's sweetened without sugar.
